title: Provide explicit authenticated HTTPS LAN access
body:
## Outcome
Provide explicit authenticated HTTPS LAN access.

## Scope and source
[September 5 handoff](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/main/docs/reference/2026-09-05-agent-handoff.md), sections 8-10. Preserve its evidence boundaries. This issue delivers the scoped portion of M5; other milestone work stays in linked issues.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Keep loopback default. Enable LAN only with authenticated sessions, trusted HTTPS, host/origin allowlists and CSRF/DNS-rebinding protections; never wildcard CORS.
- [ ] Keep credentials out of URLs/logs/source and device addresses constrained. Test unauthorized/cross-origin/replayed requests and arbitrary outgoing targets.
- [ ] Document secure desktop/phone setup, guest-Wi-Fi isolation, and Windows/WSL routing separately from device errors. No automatic firewall/router changes or direct internet exposure.
- [ ] Validate two authenticated browser clients and persistence across refresh. Actual phone and Pixoo verification remains M6; no claim of PWA install/offline support.

## Dependencies
- #10

## Verification approach
Use focused unit/integration/browser checks appropriate to the criteria, actual red/green evidence for executable changes, and the repository CI. No hardware or installation side effects are authorized by issue creation.

## Delivery target
Source-only.

## Deferral decision
The user chose to keep the application localhost-only and postpone authenticated HTTPS LAN access. Revisit this issue when access from a phone or another computer is requested. Its acceptance criteria remain outstanding; do not enable LAN access without completing them. No application or host configuration changes were made.

## Priority and access decision
Deferred for mobile or another-computer browser access. Local Codex controls retain their own machine-client authentication in #24; deferring this issue does not disable that requirement. [divoom-app-upgrade#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/43) owns future browser acceptance. Local #12/#26 acceptance does not depend on this issue.

body:
## Outcome
Validate local physical playback, recovery, and soak reliability.

## Scope and source
[September 5 handoff](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/main/docs/reference/2026-09-05-agent-handoff.md), sections 9-11. Preserve its evidence boundaries. This issue delivers the scoped portion of M6; other milestone work stays in linked issues.

## Current approved disposition

The owner approved the prepared narrow deferral after asking to wrap up visual testing. [#55](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/55) now owns effective variable GIF timing qualification. A remained ambiguous, B looked equal despite asymmetric requested delays, and the equal-500-ms control looked equal. These observations remain unverified timing evidence, not a pass. The normal application profile stays uniform 500 ms; no application behavior or product specification changes with this disposition.

All remaining physical observations for this issue are complete. The recorded approximate 28-second still reading remains outside the agreed 29-31-second tolerance; two later readings were 30.3 seconds. The failed three-play transition and later known flashing remain accepted under #52. Screen-on content retention remains a separately accepted limitation with an observed explicit-Resume recovery. The approved deferral changes only the variable-timing component. It preserves every other criterion, tolerance, observation and delivery gate.

All physical helpers are closed, with final blue 30 owner-confirmed. No additional physical operation is part of closeout. Final hardware documentation is committed in candidate `267df1d6aa05032c54cea1a3f9f856b7fe2a3fa0`. Both independent reviews found no P0-P3 findings, and all five current-head PR jobs passed in [run 34293736877](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/34293736877). [PR #54](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/pull/54) merged at `7c1204fd2516df86c706bae7c9498a5ee1bb749b`, with a tree identical to reviewed head. [Merged-main run 34294175210](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/34294175210) passed all five configured jobs. Source and scoped physical acceptance are complete. [Final guide PR #79](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/79) merged at `8064537639d7a91a66657cdbce9a63654e41b80c`, preserving the independently reviewed tree. All twelve merged-main jobs passed in [run 34295211810](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/34295211810). The guide records completed #12 and open timing follow-up #55. Guide synchronization and the authorized delivery are complete. The records below are dated execution history; earlier pending-approval or blocker statements describe those earlier checkpoints.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Obtain user approval for display-changing tests and a normal-cadence soak. Capture model/firmware and tested profile without committing private identifiers.
- [x] Observe 30-second image dwell, numbered GIFs at several total-play counts, upload gaps and play-boundary error under the current uniform-500-ms profile; retain the agreed tolerances and accepted defect #52. Effective variable timing is deferred by explicit owner approval to #55.
- [x] Validate pause/resume restart, skip during loading, stop, brightness, screen off/on, user-assisted disconnect/reconnect and server restart without stale commands.
- [x] Run a user-approved soak of at least 60 minutes AND 100 transitions; report latency distribution, artifacts, freezes/recoveries and server resource growth.
- [x] Record dated user-observed local playback results and source revision in hardware-validation documentation. Authenticated phone access and continued playback after phone close/lock are preserved in [divoom-app-upgrade#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/43) and do not block this local acceptance issue.
- [x] Report every check pass/fail/blocked. Keep this issue open if hardware acceptance is pending; describe simulator-only completion as software complete with hardware verification pending.

## Dependencies
- #4
- [divoom-app-upgrade#42](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/42) for physical adapter integration in the application.
- #10 for local startup/operations.

## Verification approach
Record dated device/user observations and separate automated source checks as specified above. No hardware actions are authorized by issue creation.

## Delivery target
Source plus separately authorized physical acceptance.

## Priority and access decision
Prioritize local playback and recovery; perform the normal-cadence soak only after the user approves its schedule and limits. Local Codex command-path acceptance is #26 and can complete independently of this broad soak. Remote browser acceptance is deferred in [divoom-app-upgrade#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/43); #11 is no longer a prerequisite here.

## Earlier delivery assessment, September 8, 2026

Coordinator: current authorized deliver-work session. Fresh base: `d51ce01dbe7be66322f58f333465d49f405bdd6d`; branch: `codex/gh-12-physical-acceptance`. The pre-start audit found no dedicated #12 branch, PR, OpenSpec change or execution record. #4, #42 and #10 are complete; #26 is narrower prior acceptance.

The owner supplied the exact target privately, identified Pixoo64, accepted the staged tests and proposed timing tolerances, and is available for the observation checkpoints. Firmware remains unknown. Use synthetic content, one WSL backend/writer, private runtime storage, and the existing profile for initial checks. Restore known brightness/screen state when reachable; prior artwork is not guaranteed recoverable.

Complexity medium: playback/control/restart and prolonged observations. Uncertainty high: visible timing and variable-delay qualification remain unmeasured. Impact medium: temporary visible content/settings changes and owner-assisted recovery. Supported-profile checks are ready; variable timing is a bounded investigation before any expanded-profile operation. No incompatible profile or unsupported hardware behavior is assumed.

Evidence mapping: criterion 1 uses this session authorization plus private target/profile records; criterion 2 uses generated fixtures, measured state timing and dated user observations; criterion 3 uses staged controls and owner-assisted device/backend recovery; criterion 4 requires both 60 minutes and 100 transitions, a 75-minute cap, latency/artifact records and resource samples; criteria 5-6 use a reviewed hardware-validation update with explicit pass/fail/blocked dispositions. Accepted proposed tolerances: 30-second dwell within 1 second; GIF play boundary within one 500 ms frame; loading interruptions require separate owner assessment.

Physical results remain pending. The user reports Actions budget restored; rerun and verify all configured jobs, preserving independent Standards/Specification review and guarded squash merge. Deliver-work is the installed successor to the retired github-delivery name. Reassess on profile discoveries, unacceptable output, uncertain writes or changed scope. Final source delivery includes the required linked hub guide synchronization.

## Validation checkpoint, September 8, 2026

The Actions budget fix is verified: [main run 34255897665, attempt 2](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/34255897665) passed all five configured jobs at `d51ce01dbe7be66322f58f333465d49f405bdd6d`. Local Node 24.20.0 `npm ci` and `npm run check` passed, including 270 application tests, 10 workflow tests, 11 specifications and 12 archives. Local HTTP checks require command-local loopback proxy exclusions in this execution environment; no product tests were changed.

Original synthetic 64x64 fixtures and the staged playlists were prepared. Independent fixture decoding confirmed two 500 ms GIF frames; simulator import and a one-play-to-still transition succeeded. Source remains unchanged at the base revision.

The physical application backend acquired the standard exclusive target lock and passed startup health. Its one read-only probe failed with `offline`, `priorEffects:none`. Direct TCP diagnosis returned `ENETUNREACH`; a final read-only proxy request was explicitly blocked because the session sandbox rejects local/private network addresses, including after an escalation request. The backend was stopped cleanly. No display-changing command was sent. This does not establish a device or LAN failure outside the session.

Permission retry: after the owner selected the device-development profile, the approved target answered a read-only channel request through the configured proxy with HTTP 200 and device error_code 0. The previous private-address permission block is cleared.

Execution blocker resolved: Codex ran the normal rebuilt application's read-only probe successfully at clean commit `b490290d4896065253571dbcf39c3a78d74b0949`. The application returned `available:true` and `connected:true`, read the channel and known display settings, and closed cleanly. No display-changing command was sent. The owner no longer needs to run the manual terminal probe. Existing hardware authorization remains valid; visible timing, controls/recovery, variable-delay qualification and soak acceptance remain pending.

The pinned local Chromium download is separately allowlist-blocked, and cached Chrome cannot launch under the session socket restriction. Hosted pinned-browser checks passed; no local visual pass is claimed. Keep #12 open. Independent final reviews, candidate PR/main checks, physical acceptance and companion guide synchronization remain future delivery gates.


## Codex execution compatibility, September 8, 2026

The owner requested that Codex run the commands without a manual terminal handoff. The approved read-only application probe still fails after escalation. The transport creates an unconfigured per-request HTTP agent, which omits Node's explicitly enabled environment proxy. Implement a bounded compatibility fix that inherits the configured Node proxy while preserving fresh request connections, fixed private device destination/port/path, response validation, cancellation and the serialized writer. Test proxy opt-in, direct operation and NO_PROXY with isolated loopback fixtures, then repeat the normal application's read-only probe from Codex.

No product specification delta is required: this restores execution through operator-configured networking while preserving the existing device command, admission, lifecycle and evidence contracts. Document the connection route and its cancellation limits. No Codex permission policy, router/firewall, firmware, automatic retry or display-changing scope is added. Broader #12 hardware acceptance and normal delivery gates remain pending.


The connection fix is committed on `codex/gh-12-physical-acceptance`; latest head is `15b0820eaf14e6d61da44e299b2407f339bfe6c1`. The follow-up commit only declares Node >=24.5 <25 in package metadata and documentation, matching the introduction of Node HTTP proxy support. The lockfile was regenerated with npm; the installed runtime was not changed. `npm ci` and the full `npm run check` passed on Node 24.20.0 at this head: 273 application tests, 10 workflow tests, 11 specifications and 12 archives. The new test reproduced the incorrect direct route before the fix and now verifies proxy opt-in, direct operation, NO_PROXY and separate connections.

This resolves the Codex execution compatibility substep. It does not complete #12 or establish physical playback accuracy. Candidate hosted CI, final acceptance/review, publication/merge and companion hub guide synchronization remain pending. The remaining variable-timing qualification requires a bounded observed profile before that criterion can pass.


## Physical acceptance checkpoint, September 8, 2026 UTC

Tested application source: `15b0820eaf14e6d61da44e299b2407f339bfe6c1`, Node 24.20.0, existing Pixoo64 smoke profile through the approved command proxy and one normal application writer. The owner confirmed the expected white 30/border on blue and one red 1 / green 2 cycle followed by the still.

The three-play test exposed unexpected output. The owner reported three complete cycles followed by several rapid extra 1 / 2 cycles before the blue still. The expected visible sequence failed. Recorded backend intervals were 3000.159 ms playing and 195.791 ms transitioning to still readiness; these are state-derived intervals, not visible-burst measurements. No session error or reconnect appeared. Playback was stopped and the physical backend closed. Brightness and screen state were not changed.

At the initial stop, five plays, controls, recovery and soak had not run. The owner has since accepted the transition artifact as nonblocking, as recorded below. Variable timing remains separately unqualified. The hardware-validation draft retains the failed visible observation; it is not promoted to a pass.

A local full-application reproduction with the same assets/policy issued exactly five requests: ID query, two GIF frames, ID query, one still frame. All uploaded frames retained 500 ms timing and the expected RGB hashes/ID association. This software run does not explain the physical burst. Independent inspection and 53 relevant source tests likewise found no duplicate upload or deliberate speed change. No firmware defect is asserted.

The owner authorized one bounded traced repeat and reported the rapid burst again. Exactly five physical requests completed with error_code 0 and no retry: an ID query, two GIF frames under returned ID 6, another query and the still under ID 7. Every frame used PicSpeed 500 and the expected rendered RGB hash. The second query began 3004.108 ms after the final GIF response; the query/still-upload interval was 205.987 ms. These include trace overhead and HTTP completion, not visible timing. The backend stopped and closed. Extra application uploads, changed requested speed and reused IDs do not explain this recorded run.


## Accepted defect and continuation decision, September 8, 2026

The owner requested a backlog defect and explicitly accepted the rapid GIF-to-still flashing as nonblocking for moving forward. [Defect #52](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/52) now owns investigation and correction. The observed three-play sequence remains failed with this accepted known-defect disposition; no root cause or fix is claimed.

Continue the remaining approved supported-profile tests, including five plays, controls, recovery and the bounded soak after the shorter checks. Recurrence of the same known burst will be recorded without reopening that resolved continuation decision. New uncertain writes, conflicting writers or other unexpected output still require assessment. All other acceptance criteria remain unchanged. Variable timing is still a separate qualification gap; final evidence, independent reviews, candidate/main CI and guide synchronization remain required.


## Resumed tests and new observation checkpoint, September 8, 2026 UTC

The owner confirmed five normal 1 / 2 cycles followed by blue 30 with the known flashing. Backend GIF dwell was 5000.601 ms and still loading was 199.978 ms. Defect #52 remains accepted and nonblocking.

The owner also confirmed blue remained during pause, changed to the numbered GIF about 30 seconds after resume, and GIF content remained after Stop. Backend pause lasted 50.877 seconds; resume gave the still a fresh 30.002 seconds, followed by 366.962 ms GIF loading. Exact visible dwell was not measured.

The next batch submitted Skip 4.459 ms after the GIF entered loading; that GIF never reached backend playing. The API then accepted 20% brightness, screen off/on and restoration to 100%. Screen-on left playback paused, and the device probe returned brightness 100%, screen on and channel 1. The owning backend closed cleanly; a new backend restored the same session/item paused with connectivity unknown and performed only local health/status/catalog reads.

The owner subsequently reported random GIFs and said they did not see the last test execute. Skip, brightness/screen and unchanged physical content across backend restart are therefore unconfirmed. The restarted backend was closed immediately without another device command. The onset and cause of the non-test content are unknown; API success is not a visual pass.

Current physical checkpoint: resolve or explicitly disposition this separate unexpected-content observation before more display commands. It is not covered by the accepted rapid-flashing defect. Device disconnect/reconnect, variable timing and soak remain unexecuted. Confirmed observations are retained; no additional acceptance criterion is marked complete.


## Isolated screen off/on observation, September 8, 2026 UTC

The owner reports the Divoom app closed and no known active external controller. They authorized a step-by-step repeat that omitted Skip, brightness changes and backend restart during the observation interval. The same application source and normal exclusive backend were used.

The blue still was uploaded once. Its still-only playlist completed after a 30001.476 ms backend playing-to-idle interval, and the owner confirmed blue 30 was still visible afterward. The owner confirmed a dark screen after Off, then reported "Random GIFs return." after On. The player remained paused and no replacement artwork was submitted. The backend closed after the final observation. Brightness was unchanged.

This isolates screen off/on as a sufficient trigger for the content change in the observed sequence. The internal device cause and precise return timing remain unknown. The screen controls visibly operated, but uploaded content was not retained across the cycle. Source behavior follows the current contract: screen-on does not resume playback or upload artwork. The earlier missed Skip/brightness test remains unconfirmed.

This finding is separate from accepted flashing defect #52. The owner explicitly accepted screen-on returning random GIFs while the player stays paused as a known limitation for #12, and authorized one explicit Resume to reload the retained content. This resolves the screen-retention continuation decision. The observed loss of uploaded content remains recorded; automatic artwork restoration is not added. Device disconnect/reconnect, variable timing and soak remain pending, along with final delivery gates.


## Supported-profile controls and recovery complete, September 8, 2026 UTC

The owner confirmed explicit Resume restored blue 30 after the accepted screen-on limitation. The same retained session resumed, with a 223.047 ms backend loading interval. Separate observed brightness checks confirmed dimming at requested 20% and restoration; the device probe reported 100%, screen on.

The isolated Skip repeat submitted Next 4.112 ms after GIF loading began. The skipped GIF never reached backend playing, and the owner confirmed blue 30 stayed visible without a delayed GIF start. A separate backend restart, without screen toggles, preserved the visible blue still and restored the same session/item paused. Only local health/status/catalog reads were made after restart.

For device recovery, the owner unplugged power. One Resume command produced bounded reconnect handling followed by offline/error with paused intent after 15.089 seconds. Stop retired that attempt before power was restored. After reboot the owner saw native GIFs. A new probe confirmed connectivity, 100% brightness and screen on while playback remained idle/stopped. A fresh Resume cleared the error and restored blue 30, confirmed by the owner, with 284.255 ms backend loading. Final Stop and backend close completed. No delayed test-content replay was observed before fresh intent.

Criterion 3 is complete with the accepted screen-retention limitation and its verified explicit-Resume path. Defect #52 remains an accepted nonblocking visual defect. Precise visible timing is separate from the state-derived numbers above. The 60-minute/100-transition soak and variable-timing qualification remain pending. Private soak-helper simulator checks and independent preflight review are underway; no physical soak has started. Final source/review/CI/guide delivery gates remain required.


## Physical soak started, September 8, 2026 UTC

The already approved soak started at 22:17:44 UTC on application source `15b0820eaf14e6d61da44e299b2407f339bfe6c1`. The normal device backend holds the target lock and alternates the synthetic still and two-frame 500 ms GIF, each with a 30-second duration. Completion requires at least 60 minutes AND 100 ordered completed transitions; 75 minutes is an incomplete-run cap. The reviewed private runner records SSE states/loading intervals and server resources, then sends Stop and closes on completion, interruption or unexpected state. Both independent helper reviews cleared the startup/revision fixes after simulator regressions.

Startup was admitted against the exact approved playlist revision. No soak pass or physical timing accuracy is claimed yet. Owner observations, final duration/transition count, resource analysis and clean shutdown remain pending. Variable timing remains outside the currently qualified application profile and is still an unresolved criterion.


## Soak observations and next experiment approval, September 8, 2026

The owner confirmed the expected alternating blue still and numbered GIF during the running soak. They clarified the known transition burst: blue 30 briefly interleaves with red 1 / green 2 before settling. Defect #52 now records that detail. Visible blue dwell was first reported as about 28 seconds, then measured at 30.3 seconds in each of two repeats. Two readings fall within the agreed 29-31-second range; preserve the earlier approximate outlier and unquantified human measurement uncertainty.

The owner explicitly approved the reviewed variable timing feasibility sequence after the soak closes: [500,1000], [1000,500], then [500,500] ms for the same two numbered frames. Each stage uploads the GIF once, holds for 15 seconds, uploads the blue still once, and closes, with at most five protocol requests and a 45-second external cap. Each stage has an owner observation checkpoint. Both independent helper reviews cleared and fixture failure/interruption checks passed. No variable-delay physical stage has run yet. The experimental profile remains unverified and the application profile unchanged; protocol feasibility alone cannot complete normal-application variable-timing acceptance.

Supplementary local browser verification now passed all 52 application tests using installed Chromium149 headless shell with the repository assertions and an explicit private executable override. The generated companion work guide also passed its browser checks. Full desktop Chromium still fails at its restricted process-singleton socket. Candidate hosted CI must retain its pinned browser and all required jobs; no test or permission-policy exception is adopted.


## Delivery checkpoint, September 8, 2026

[Draft PR #54](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/pull/54) publishes compatibility head `15b0820eaf14e6d61da44e299b2407f339bfe6c1` while physical evidence is collected. [PR run 34287878983](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/34287878983), attempt 1, passed all five configured jobs, including the pinned Chromium browser suite, against PR #54 and base `459968ef11a8fb4558b3c76411e14d4564d6929f`. This is preflight CI for the draft head; final changes require current reviews and CI.

The device route, browser execution and exact physical experiment scope are now available and agreed, so remove the execution blocked label. Remaining work is in progress: finish the running soak, perform the approved variable-timing feasibility stages and assess their normal-application implications, finalize evidence, reconcile the newer main, obtain final independent reviews/current CI, and complete the companion guide delivery. No acceptance criterion is waived or newly checked at this checkpoint.


## Soak runtime completed, September 8, 2026 UTC

The device-mode soak completed from 22:17:44 to 23:17:46 UTC at source `15b0820eaf14e6d61da44e299b2407f339bfe6c1`: 60 minutes 2.192 seconds, 119 ordered transitions and 120 playing visits. Both required runtime thresholds passed before the 75-minute cap. The backend reported no error or recovery state; Stop and close succeeded. Independent analysis of the complete private log matched the runner receipt.

Across 120 backend loading intervals, median was 246.307 ms, 95th percentile 379.620 ms, maximum 1105.055 ms. Still/GIF medians were 173.784/332.166 ms. The 119 completed backend dwell intervals ranged from 29999.815 to 30001.208 ms. These are SSE-derived intervals, not visible display timings.

RSS was 88.703 MiB at startup, 88.113 MiB at the final periodic sample and 88.363 MiB after close. Median RSS rose 6.750 MiB between minutes 5-10 and the final five minutes. Periodic peak was 104.168 MiB; process-reported peak was 113.656 MiB. Average sampled CPU was about 0.106% of one core. The application and recorder share a process; this bounded run does not prove absence of leaks.

The owner confirmed normal alternation at the midpoint. Closing visual confirmation is requested and remains pending; criterion 4 is therefore not checked yet. The hardware-validation draft records the completed runtime, measurements and this evidence boundary. No variable-timing stage has run. Existing approval for the reviewed stages remains valid; observe each before the next.


## Soak visual acceptance and timing experiment checkpoint, September 8, 2026 UTC

The owner confirmed: "Yes the display kept alternating through the end with only the known flashing." Together with the completed 60-minute/119-transition run, latency/resource analysis and clean shutdown, this completes criterion 4 with accepted defect #52. No new freeze or unexpected content was reported. The dated hardware-validation draft records the evidence; publication and final delivery gates remain pending.

All three previously approved variable-timing protocol stages have now run once at source `15b0820eaf14e6d61da44e299b2407f339bfe6c1`. Each sent exactly five requests, received error_code 0 for all five and closed its adapter. Traces preserved the synthetic frame hashes, order and requested PicSpeed values. Each held its GIF for 15 seconds before one blue-still upload. No extra physical backend remains running.

Stage A requested red 1 at 500 ms and green 2 at 1000 ms. The owner felt red 1 lasted longer but explicitly said they could be mistaken, then confirmed blue 30. This is ambiguous, not a timing pass or a proven inversion. Stage B reversed those values; the owner reported that neither frame lasted longer and they seemed equal. The expected asymmetric timing was not demonstrated. B's still upload was acknowledged without a separate visual confirmation. The equal-500-ms control completed its requests and awaits the owner's relative-timing and final-blue observations.

The application profile remains unchanged at uniform 500 ms. No hardware cause is asserted, and no wider profile is qualified from HTTP success. Criterion 2 remains open; its variable-timing outcome requires assessment after the control observation. Existing acceptance of flashing and screen retention does not waive this separate criterion.


## Physical testing paused after completed control, September 8, 2026 UTC

The owner confirmed the equal-duration control looked equal and final blue 30 was showing. All three approved protocol stages completed and closed. A remains ambiguous, B did not demonstrate the requested asymmetry, and the control looked equal. Effective variable timing remains unverified. The current uniform-500-ms application profile is unchanged; no cause or wider hardware support is claimed.

The owner then stepped away and explicitly paused further visual testing while authorizing independent work to continue. All physical processes were already closed. No further device operation is planned in their absence. Continue source reconciliation, documentation, automated checks and PR preparation.

The completed evidence was committed as `989e0af23ddbe20d6150cb4da73a0c23d4e68ac3`; merging current main `459968ef11a8fb4558b3c76411e14d4564d6929f` produced clean candidate `74ffc2eb7af1af9c0fdc76246422dd3470a035e2`. Physical tests remain attributed to `15b0820eaf14e6d61da44e299b2407f339bfe6c1`. Fresh local checks and independent candidate reviews are being prepared.

A private draft proposes moving only variable-timing qualification into a dedicated follow-up, while preserving the supported-profile results and every other delivery gate. This is not an accepted scope change: no follow-up issue has been created and criterion 2 remains unchanged and open. The owner can decide when they return. The draft PR remains ineligible for final acceptance/merge until the required disposition and remaining review/CI/guide gates are resolved.


## Independent work completed during physical-test pause, September 8, 2026 UTC

[Draft PR #54](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/pull/54) now publishes clean candidate `74ffc2eb7af1af9c0fdc76246422dd3470a035e2`, reconciled with main `459968ef11a8fb4558b3c76411e14d4564d6929f`. It includes the proxy compatibility fix and dated physical evidence. Node 24.20.0 setup and full checks passed: 276 application tests across 40 files, 10 workflow tests, 12 specifications and 13 archives. All 52 supplementary browser tests passed, with desktop/mobile screenshots inspected.

Independent Standards and Specification reviews of that same committed comparison found no P0-P3 candidate defects. Specification independently reconciled the raw observations, soak metrics and remaining acceptance gap. [PR run 34291316108](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/34291316108) passed all five configured jobs at the current head and base, including hosted pinned Chromium. No provider review, general comment or unresolved review thread was present in the current readback.

The [hub guide checkpoint PR #78](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/78) merged at `a5e03a031583cabab0941804df26092a51b66a46`, with a tree matching reviewed head `03d40e496b14e2df7c005d5898fa73bd09c27ef2`. Its generator/maintenance/browser checks, both independent reviews and all twelve PR jobs passed. [Main run 34292448938](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/34292448938) then passed all twelve jobs at the merged revision. The existing document-specific human-approval exemption was verified in hub main and PR #76; no new waiver or device authority was inferred. Later #12 source/status changes still require guide reconciliation before full completion.

Remaining blocker: effective variable timing is unverified and the owner paused further visual testing. The uniform-500-ms profile remains unchanged. The private follow-up proposal is a concrete draft only; the owner has not accepted a deferral, and no new issue or reduced criterion was applied. All physical helpers are closed and final blue 30 was owner-confirmed. No further device operation ran while the owner was away.

Keep this issue open with status:in-progress and blocked, and keep PR #54 draft. The execution/network/CI blockers are resolved. The next required input is the owner's timing-qualification disposition when they return, followed by any resulting implementation/evidence changes, refreshed gates, source merge/main CI and final guide reconciliation. This checkpoint does not close #12 or claim complete hardware acceptance.


## Source and scoped physical completion

All six current acceptance criteria are satisfied under the explicitly approved variable-timing deferral to #55. The current uniform-500-ms profile is unchanged. Dated hardware documentation is published on main; the failed three-play sequence, approximate 28-second still outlier, ambiguous variable experiment and accepted screen-retention limitation remain recorded. Known flashing stays open in #52. Variable timing remains unverified in #55.

Local Node 24.20.0 checks passed 276 application tests, 10 workflow tests and 52 browser tests. Inventory is 12 specifications and 13 archives. The final documentation-only delta passed diff checks; both fresh independent reviews and all five final PR jobs passed. All five merged-revision main jobs then passed. No further hardware operation, installation or phone-access acceptance is claimed.

The earlier hub guide checkpoint PR #78 and final reconciliation PR #79 are both merged and verified. Both final guide reviews found no P0-P3 findings, all twelve PR jobs passed, and all twelve merged-main jobs passed. title: Connect ChatGPT to the local MCP server through a private tunnel
body:
## Shared-hub ownership
Keep remote connectivity deferred. Reuse [agent-device-hub#7](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/7) through a qualified Pixoo-local endpoint or explicitly selected hub gateway. Document the deployment before implementation. A tunnel is not needed for local hooks, monitoring or the unified local UI.

## Outcome
Connect ChatGPT web to the local Pixoo application's MCP tools through an authenticated private connection.

## Scope and source
Refine the existing remote-control backlog issue for the requested ChatGPT integration. Reuse the MCP endpoint from #24 and its shared application services. Prefer OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel, with a client running beside the local backend and reaching OpenAI through outbound HTTPS. The local app and Pixoo remain private.

This is follow-on work outside the mixed-playlist MVP. #11 continues to own authenticated browser LAN access; [divoom-app-upgrade#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/43) owns remote browser acceptance and #12 owns local physical playback/soak. Neither a LAN listener nor completion of physical soak testing is required to develop this outbound MCP path. Public plugin distribution, general remote browser control, and other VPN/hosting options remain outside this implementation slice.

Official documentation checked September 6, 2026: [Secure MCP Tunnel](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/secure-mcp-tunnels), [ChatGPT developer mode](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/developer-mode), and [MCP](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp). Recheck these sources when implementation starts.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Resolve the connection/authentication design before marking ready. Document target ChatGPT developer-mode availability, Platform tunnel permissions and organization/workspace association, runtime credential handling, and how the tunnel authenticates to the local MCP endpoint. If the supported route is unavailable, record the exact missing prerequisite and proposed alternative for user decision.
- [ ] Provide the source/configuration templates and runbook needed to connect a developer-mode app to the running backend through the selected private tunnel. Reuse the same MCP tools and backend queue as Codex; the bridge never talks directly to the Pixoo or launches another device-writing backend.
- [ ] Preserve loopback defaults and require an explicitly configured endpoint and credentials. Expose only the intended MCP path through the tunnel, not the rest of the web server or private media directory. Verify the bridge can authenticate locally without weakening the local MCP access checks.
- [ ] Define and test authorization at both the remote connection and local app boundary. Keep runtime keys, local credentials, private IPs, and media paths out of Git, URLs, tool results, and routine logs. Treat read-only/write annotations as client guidance, with server authorization enforced independently.
- [ ] Document start, health/readiness checks, failure diagnosis, credential rotation/revocation, disconnect, and cleanup. A stopped or revoked tunnel rejects new remote work; local app use continues. Reconnect must not blindly replay uncertain writes.
- [ ] Document that the host/backend/tunnel must remain running for ChatGPT calls. Client disconnection does not own or stop playback. Keep app deployment and persistent host startup aligned with #10 without adding an always-on installation to source delivery.
- [ ] Provide a simulator-only end-to-end runbook for tool discovery, approved writes, failures, and disconnect/reconnect. Actual ChatGPT account setup and live client/device evidence are completed in [divoom-app-upgrade#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/44), with unavailable access recorded there rather than claimed from mocks.
- [ ] Prepare the issue-linked OpenSpec proposal, affected capability deltas, tasks, design, and ADR for the transport/auth boundary before implementation. Do not add public ingress or change router/firewall settings as an automatic fallback.

Planned OpenSpec change: `gh-17-chatgpt-private-mcp`.

## Verification approach
Use isolated test credentials, a local MCP test server/client, and a fake tunnel transport where practical to verify target restriction, authentication, disconnects, revocation, and duplicate-request behavior. Separate tests of our wrapper/configuration from claims about the external tunnel service. Source tests must pass without external accounts or a device.

Run Node 24 `npm ci` and all repository checks applicable to changed source, HTTP/startup behavior, and OpenSpec artifacts, including `npm run check` and `npm run test:browser` for application changes. Require all configured PR/main CI. Live ChatGPT setup and acceptance belong to [divoom-app-upgrade#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/44).

## Dependencies
- #24 for the authenticated local MCP endpoint.
- Verified target account/workspace permissions and a settled transport/auth design before readiness.

Additional shared prerequisites:
- [agent-device-hub#7](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/7)

## Related work
#25 adds media/playlist tools and can proceed independently of this connection work. #10 supplies shared deployment guidance when available; this issue owns tunnel-specific lifecycle instructions. [divoom-app-upgrade#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/44) owns remote client/device verification and depends on this issue. The former #12 prerequisite is replaced by #24 because source delivery of an outbound MCP connection does not require phone/LAN or soak acceptance.

Source-only. Account registration, key creation, tunnel installation, personal app configuration, and hardware actions require the later explicitly authorized setup/acceptance work.

title: Fix rapid extra GIF flashes before the next still image
body:
## Observed and expected behavior

During physical acceptance for #12 on September 8, 2026, the owner observed three normal red 1 / green 2 cycles, followed by several rapid extra cycles before the blue 30 still appeared. The rapid burst repeated in one separately authorized traced run. Expected behavior is the requested normal cadence followed by the still, without the rapid extra flashing.

The owner accepted this as a known defect and explicitly said it must not block continuing #12. Preserve the failed observation in acceptance evidence. This issue tracks investigation and correction; it does not claim a firmware cause or a completed fix.

## Reproduction

1. With separately authorized access to a Pixoo64, run one device-mode application backend using the normal target lock and an isolated synthetic library.
2. Use application source `15b0820eaf14e6d61da44e299b2407f339bfe6c1`, Node 24.20.0 and profile `pixoo64-smoke-2026-09-06`. Firmware was unknown. The observed session used the configured HTTP proxy.
3. Play a two-frame 64x64 GIF with red 1 and green 2, each delayed 500 ms, using a three-total-plays policy. Follow it with a blue 30 still with a 30-second duration, repeat off.
4. Observe the transition after the three normal cycles. The owner reported rapid extra flashes before the still on both runs. Their duration has not been visually measured.

The traced repeat sent exactly five requests: `Draw/GetHttpGifId`, two `Draw/SendHttpGif` frames, another ID query, then one still frame. The GIF used returned ID 6 and the still ID 7. Every frame used `PicSpeed:500` and the expected rendered RGB hash. All responses reported `error_code:0`; no retries or rejected requests occurred. The second ID query began 3004.108 ms after the last GIF response. The ID query plus still upload took 205.987 ms, including tracing and HTTP completion. These are request timings, not visible-burst measurements.

A local full-application fixture likewise sent the expected five requests. No duplicate application upload, changed requested speed or reused animation ID explains the traced run. The display's internal behavior remains unknown.

## Scope

Diagnose and correct the rapid flashing during the two-frame GIF to one-frame still handoff. Preserve the serialized writer, fresh-intent recovery, immutable media and truthful timing estimates. Assess any protocol/profile change against physical evidence before implementation. Do not assume that resetting IDs, changing firmware or adding arbitrary delays is a valid fix.

Broader transition improvements remain in #16. This is a specific reproduced defect, not a duplicate of that exploratory enhancement. Private device addresses, runtime libraries and raw receipts stay outside Git.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce the reported burst with separately authorized physical observation and identify its cause or document an evidence-supported device limitation.
- [ ] If a supported correction exists, implement it with a meaningful regression check covering the identified cause and adjacent handoffs.
- [ ] Observe one-, three- and five-play sequences followed by the still without the rapid burst after the correction; report visible timing separately from HTTP success and state timing.
- [ ] Preserve cancellation, one-writer ownership, supported frame delays and failure handling; pass required source checks and independent reviews.
- [ ] Update dated hardware evidence with source revision, observed results and remaining limitations. If no supported fix exists, obtain an explicit disposition instead of claiming a pass.

## Verification approach

Use the synthetic reproduction and a bounded request trace. Pair software checks with owner-observed physical transitions. Any further physical session needs its own applicable authorization. Issue creation authorizes no display changes or firmware/network changes.

## Dependencies and priority

Found during #12; related to #16. This defect is backlog work and is explicitly nonblocking for #12 under the owner's September 8 decision. No prerequisite implementation issue is currently identified. Reassess scope and the causal evidence before marking ready.

## Delivery target

Source plus separately authorized physical-device verification.


## Further owner observation, September 8, 2026

During the approved #12 soak, the owner clarified that blue 30 briefly interleaves with the red 1 / green 2 frames before the display settles on solid blue 30. The two items retain 30-second duration policies and the GIF uses two 500 ms frames. This describes the recurring accepted transition burst; no root cause or correction is established.

Two subsequent owner stopwatch readings, from solid blue appearance until the numbered GIF replaced it, were 30.3 seconds each. An earlier approximate reading was 28 seconds. Preserve all three readings and their human measurement limits. These visible readings are separate from backend SSE dwell measurements.

title: Expose user-entered playlist names through the Pixoo integration extension
body:
## Outcome

Expose the user-entered name of each discoverable saved playlist through the Pixoo integration extension, so the shared BUNNY frontend can label playlist selection instead of showing bare IDs.

## Scope and accepted definition

The accepted general-control definition is [Hub #31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31), recorded in the hub as ADR 0005 (`docs/decisions/0005-general-device-controls.md`). Controller v1 exposes up to the first 100 saved playlist IDs without names and remains unchanged. This issue adds an additive field to the Pixoo-owned `pixoo-integration` extension under a new compatible minor version, with explicit consumer negotiation.

This issue is non-blocking for the hub's Pixoo general-control UI. That UI is accepted with IDs alone and shows names only after it consumes the new extension version.

## Accepted behavior

- A playlist name is included only when it was entered by the user in the Pixoo application. Names derived from filenames, media titles or paths are omitted, not substituted.
- Names follow the shared label bound of at most 80 Unicode characters and contain no credentials, paths or private metadata.
- The mapping is keyed by the same playlist IDs and catalog revision that controller v1 discovery uses, so a stale name cannot be paired with a different playlist.
- Browser and local MCP routes are unchanged. Reads add no device writes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** The extension snapshot carries the additive name field under a new minor version; existing consumers of the current version keep working. The exact issue-linked OpenSpec change records the delta.
- [ ] **AC2.** Validation rejects names above the bound and never includes names that are not user-entered; tests cover a playlist without a user-entered name.
- [ ] **AC3.** Names and IDs are consistent with the catalog revision in the same snapshot; a catalog change advances the revision.
- [ ] **AC4.** A linked Hub companion PR updates the hub's pinned Pixoo integration fixtures and compatibility record.

## Required source prerequisites

- [Hub #31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31): general-control definition, accepted 2026-09-22.
- [#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/37) and [#33](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/33): controller API and integration extension, closed.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-22, against divoom-app-upgrade `main` and the accepted Hub #31 decisions.

- **Complexity: low.** One additive read field on an existing versioned extension.
- **Uncertainty: low.** Whether Pixoo stores an explicit user-entered playlist name must be confirmed in the code before the field is specified; if names are ever auto-derived, the omission rule applies.
- **Impact: low.** Read-only data; a wrong name is a labeling defect, not a device effect.

**Readiness:** ready. **Review:** independent Standards and Specification reviews with a privacy check on name provenance.

## Planning and delivery

Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. Use the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change, proportionate executable checks, isolated work, independent review, guarded merge and merged-revision CI. Keep private media, credentials and runtime state out of Git. This issue does not authorize installation or device operations.

The hub changed this in [agent-device-hub#169](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/169) (`ad5aef8`, current hub `main` `a76b22d`). It retired the `updates.md` ledger and made the guide an intentional, dated publication. A device repository needs a linked hub PR only when its authorized scope includes a guide update. Coordinators and reviewers here get conflicting instructions on every delivery.

Outdated text at `main` `c81bc31`:

- `AGENTS.md:90-100` ("Work guide maintenance"): the linked hub PR, `updates.md` or no-impact record, and "pending guide synchronization remains unfinished delivery work".
- `docs/sdlc.md:58-61` (hub guide checkpoints at planning, review and completion) and `docs/sdlc.md:128-140` ("Cross-project guide completion gate").
- `README.md:97` ("a linked hub PR under the SDLC completion gate").
- `.github/pull_request_template.md:29-30` (the unconditional hub-sync checklist).

## Outcome

This repository's guide-maintenance rules match the hub's current procedure.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `AGENTS.md`, `docs/sdlc.md`, README and the PR template no longer require an `updates.md` entry, a no-impact record or a hub PR for every delivery. They point to the hub procedure and state that a linked hub PR is required only when a task's authorized scope intentionally updates or publishes the guide.
2. The existing boundaries are kept: read-only and tracker-only limits, no device or hosting authority, separate source-completion/guide-revision/public-publication/live-verification claims, and "a source merge does not update the public site".
3. The repository's configured workflow and documentation checks pass.

## Reference

codex-nanoleaf made the same change in [codex-nanoleaf#70](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/70) / [PR #71](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/71) (merged `77f188d`). Its `AGENTS.md`, `docs/sdlc.md` "Cross-project work guide" section, README and conditional PR-template section can serve as the model. Adapt them to this repository's own conventions.

## Planning

Documentation maintenance with no behavior delta, so no OpenSpec change is needed.

## Delivery scope

Limit this cleanup to `AGENTS.md`, `docs/sdlc.md`, `README.md` and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. No hub changes, generated guide updates, public publication, application changes, new automation, installation or device testing. Use the existing workflow checks and review the instructions for contradictions. Existing review and configured CI gates still apply.

## Completion evidence

Delivered in [PR #69](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/pull/69), merged as `b7d4762bd11bbc8d15f1d04a7ef6f273f1d28050`. Both independent reviews returned no findings. title: Use shared npm and Playwright caches and fnm for Node 24 in setup guidance
body:
## Outcome

Setup guidance keeps npm and Playwright caches in their shared default locations instead of `/tmp`, and says how to select Node 24 without installing another copy.

On 2026-09-23 the WSL host's `/tmp`, a 7.6 GB RAM-backed tmpfs shared by all agent sessions, filled completely. Part of the cause was guidance that sends caches or per-task installs into `/tmp`. The Codex local-development sandbox profile now allows writes to `~/.npm` and `~/.cache/ms-playwright`, so the read-only-cache workaround is no longer needed.

## Scope

- `docs/development.md`: replace "Use `npm ci --cache /tmp/pixoo-npm-cache` if the WSL npm cache is read-only" and the `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` sandbox advice with guidance to use npm's default cache (`~/.npm`) and Playwright's default browser cache (`~/.cache/ms-playwright`), and to report a read-only cache instead of redirecting it.
- Same file: when `node --version` is not v24, prefix commands with `fnm exec --using=.nvmrc --` from the worktree root and reuse one shared Node 24 installation, as agent-device-hub documents.

Out of scope: other documentation, CI and tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- `docs/development.md` no longer recommends a `/tmp` npm cache or a sandbox browser path, and it contains the fnm note.
- `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` exit zero, and every configured CI job succeeds on the PR head and the merged main revision.

## Dependencies

None. Related: jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade#70 (cleanup after delivery).

## Verification

Local workflow checks, GitHub Actions CI, and independent Standards and Specification reviews.

## Delivery target

Merged to `main`.
